blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights two papers addressing the challenge of monitoring ongoing A/B tests, where early stopping can bias results. The first paper, 'Peeking at A/B tests: why it matters and what to do about it' (Johari et al., KDD'17), introduces the mSPRT (mixture sequential probability ratio test) as a solution within the Null Hypothesis Statistical Testing (NHST) framework, implemented in Optimizely since 2015. The paper explains the dangers of peeking at ongoing tests, which can inflate false positive rates by 5-10x, and proposes sequential analysis to control Type I errors. The second paper, 'Continuous monitoring of A/B tests without pain: optional stopping in Bayesian testing' (Deng, Lu, et al., CEUR'17), offers a Bayesian alternative, proving that continuous monitoring with proper stopping rules does not change the false discovery rate. The blog emphasizes the trade-offs between frequentist and Bayesian approaches and provides practical guidance on choosing between them.
paper_title: Peeking at A/B tests: why it matters, and what to do about it
